senses.gloss: Compares a predicate or clause stated before it to its supposed alternative, which is nullified in the predicate or clause after. Provides clarification, or implies high credibility, of either or both clauses (or predicates).
if what comes after is an interrogative word or phrase, implies that you highly doubt there is any alternative to an affirmative answer of the question
at the end of a question, hints that you think what you have said before this particle is true, although you still want to confirm it
at the end of a statement, affirms what comes before this particle and hints that you think your conversation partner was too clueless about it
